llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, granite4.1_8b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 11.6 % (median 0 %) and met the 75 % coverage threshold on just two instances, indicating very limited effectiveness despite flawless run health (zero infra or timeout errors). The failure analysis diagnosed 497 tasks (99.4 %), with cognitive mistakes accounting for 308 cases (62 %) versus 189 tool‑call issues (38 %). The most common root causes were task misunderstanding (145 failures), complete omission of required tools (no_tool_use, 117) and early termination of the reasoning chain (83), suggesting that the model frequently misinterprets multi‑step prompts and aborts before exploiting available MCP resources. While tool‑related errors such as wrong‑tool selection (63) and malformed calls (4) are present, they are eclipsed by higher‑level comprehension problems that prevent any tool invocation at all. An actionable fix is to introduce a prompt‑preprocessing layer that explicitly extracts required tool actions and validates them before the model proceeds, thereby forcing correct tool usage and reducing premature exits. This profile distinguishes granite4.1_8b_output from models that mainly struggle with API handling: its dominant weakness lies in cognitive parsing of complex tasks rather than in the mechanics of tool interaction.
